title: 第七章 草木皆兵
content_zh:
秦伯的药，确实管用。

    那几味草药调了敷上，后背的肿痛消下去不少；煎水喝了，肋上那口憋着的淤气也顺了些。第二天一早，江砚虽还浑身酸痛，到底比头一天利索了。

    他心里盘算着，得趁这几日，想办法弄清楚那支笔的门道——那是他眼下唯一可能翻盘的指望。可白天活计重，王氏又盯得紧，他根本抽不出空。好不容易挨到下午,王氏带着东西回娘家了，大伯进城办事，院里没了人看着，江砚才寻了个由头，揣上秃笔和旧纸,往村外的河滩溜去。

    村西有一条河，入了冬就冻得结结实实，河面上一层青白的厚冰，孩子们常在上头疯跑。这会儿天冷，河滩上没什么人，正是个清静地方。

    江砚寻了块背风的大石头蹲下，从怀里摸出秃笔。

    可没等他磨墨，身后就响起一阵嬉笑打闹的声音。

    “哟，废物跑这儿来藏猫猫呢？”

    江砚回头，心往下一沉。

    江狗剩带着三四个村里的半大小子，不知什么时候晃到了河边。一个个吊儿郎当，手里拎着自己绑的冰车、削尖的木棍，显然是来冰上玩的。

    为首的江狗剩一眼瞧见江砚手里那支笔，眼睛一亮，几步抢上来，一把夺了过去。

    “这是啥？”他翻来覆去看了看那截秃笔，又抢过江砚护在怀里的旧纸,展开一瞧，上头是江砚试笔留下的、歪歪扭扭的字和一团乱涂，“嚯，废物还学人写字呢？就你这身份，识俩字能当饭吃啊？”

    “还我。”江砚站起身，伸手去夺。

    那支秃笔和那几片纸，是他眼下最要紧的东西。

    江狗剩却把手一抬，举得高高的，笑嘻嘻地看着比他矮半头的江砚跳脚去够：“想要？跪下来，喊声爷爷，爷爷就还你。”

    旁边几个小子哄笑起来，跟着起哄。

    江砚没跳第二下。他停住了，盯着江狗剩，眼神冷下来：“江狗剩，别太过分。”

    这一声，又是不躲不闪、直直看过来的眼神。

    江狗剩被他看得心里头那股子说不清的别扭又冒了上来——还是昨天那种感觉，像一拳打在了石头上。这怂货，最近怎么越来越不对劲了？

    也正是这点别扭，让他恼了。
content_en:
Uncle Qin's medicine really works.

    After mixing those few herbs and applying them, the swelling and pain in my back subsided a lot. After drinking the boiled water, the stagnant qi in my ribs also became smoother. Early the next morning, although Jiang Yan was still sore all over, he was feeling better than the previous day.

    He was thinking that he would have to take advantage of these few days to figure out the secret of that pen - that was his only hope of making a comeback at the moment. But during the day, he had a lot of work to do and Mr. Wang kept a close eye on him, so he couldn't spare any time. After finally waiting until the afternoon, Mrs. Wang returned to her parents' home with her things. Her uncle went to the city to do business, and no one was watching in the courtyard. Jiang Yan found an excuse, put on a pen and old paper, and slipped to the river beach outside the village.

    There is a river in the west of the village, which freezes solidly in winter. There is a thick layer of blue-white ice on the river, and children often run wildly on it. It's cold now and there's no one on the river beach. It's a quiet place.

    Jiang Yan found a big rock with leeward wind, squatted down, and took out the bald pen from his arms.

    But before he could polish the ink, there was a sound of laughter and play behind him.

    "Hey, why are you here hiding behind a cat?"

    Jiang Yan turned around, his heart sinking.

    Jiang Goucheng and three or four young men from the village wandered to the river at some point. They were all wandering around, carrying their own ice carts and sharpened sticks in their hands, obviously coming to play on the ice.

    The leader, Jiang Goucheng, saw the pen in Jiang Yan's hand, his eyes lit up, he rushed up to it and snatched it away.

    "What is this?" He looked over and over to look at the bald pen, then grabbed the old paper that Jiang Yan was protecting in his arms, and unfolded it. On it were the crooked words and scribbles left by Jiang Yan's test pen, "Hey, how can you learn how to write like a loser? With your status, can you make a living by knowing two words?"

    "Give it back to me." Jiang Yan stood up and reached out to grab it.

    The bald pen and the pieces of paper were the most important things to him right now.

    Jiang Goucheng raised his hand high, smiling as he watched Jiang Yan, who was half a head shorter than him, jump to reach for it: "Want it? Kneel down and call grandpa, and grandpa will give it back to you."

    Several boys nearby laughed and started cheering.

    Jiang Yan did not jump a second time. He stopped and stared at Jiang Goucheng with cold eyes: "Jiang Goucheng, don't go too far."

    This time, there was another look that didn't dodge and looked straight over.

    The indescribable awkwardness in Jiang Goucheng's heart came up again when he saw him - it was still the same feeling as yesterday, like a punch on a stone. Why is this coward acting worse and worse lately?

    It was this awkwardness that annoyed him.
title_en: Chapter 7 Grass and trees are all soldiers
